subsystems.name: Soft actuators
subsystems.role: produce movement from compliant materials instead of rigid motors and gears.

subsystems.name: Compliant body and skin
subsystems.role: the structure itself bends and absorbs impacts.
parts: variable-stiffness layers (jamming granule or low-melting-point polymer)

subsystems.name: Pressure and drive supply
subsystems.role: supplies air, hydraulic fluid or high voltage to the actuators.

subsystems.name: Stretchable sensing
subsystems.role: lets the robot feel its own shape and what it is touching.

subsystems.name: Control and power electronics
subsystems.role: translates intent into valve or voltage commands without a rigid joint model to rely on.
parts: safety limits for pressure and voltage

buildSteps.title: Design the actuator geometry
buildSteps.detail: Chamber shape, fibre winding angles and wall thickness are modelled with hyperelastic material equations, since soft elastomers (modulus often 0.1–10 MPa; metals are thousands of times stiffer) stretch nonlinearly.

buildSteps.title: Make the moulds
buildSteps.detail: Moulds are machined, 3D-printed or lost-wax cast, and the inner core is designed to be dissolved or pulled out after curing.

buildSteps.title: Cast the elastomer
buildSteps.detail: Silicone or polyurethane resin is mixed, degassed under vacuum to remove bubbles, poured, and cured; layers with different stiffness are cast in sequence.

buildSteps.title: Add reinforcement and sensing
buildSteps.detail: Fibres or fabric sleeves are wrapped around the chambers to set the direction of motion, and stretchable electrodes or liquid-metal channels are embedded before the final layers cure.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the body
buildSteps.detail: Cured parts are bonded with the same silicone, pneumatic fittings are sealed, and tendons or cables are threaded where needed.

buildSteps.title: Wire up valves and electronics
buildSteps.detail: Miniature valves, pumps or high-voltage drivers are connected to each actuator, and sensor wiring is routed to the controller.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and train control
buildSteps.detail: Each unit is cycled while pressure, voltage, force and shape are logged; a learned model maps command to motion, because a soft body has no single joint angle.

buildSteps.title: Fatigue-test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Units are cycled hundreds of thousands of times to find leaks, cracks and drift before they are trusted in a wearable or surgical device.

prerequisites.tech: Soft elastomer and fibre-reinforced composite fabrication
prerequisites.why: silicones and fibre sleeves are mature; the challenge is repeatable casting at small scale.
McKibben-style muscles shortening by roughly 20–30 % of their length have been used for decades, though usually with bulky compressors.
dielectric elastomers reach large strains in the laboratory but need kilovolt drive voltages and degrade over millions of cycles.
skin-like strain and touch sensing works in prototypes but is hard to manufacture reliably.
soft robots need learned or model-free control; classical rigid-robot control does not transfer.

pathway.milestone: soft grippers, wearable assistive gloves and surgical tools in limited commercial use
pathway.unlocks: handling delicate food, produce and tissue where rigid grippers bruise or tear.

pathway.milestone: soft actuators with integrated stretchable sensing and on-board power
pathway.unlocks: untethered soft robots that can be worn all day.

pathway.milestone: variable-stiffness structures that are soft to touch but can lock rigid to lift loads
pathway.unlocks: prosthetic limbs and exoskeletons that are both comfortable and strong.

pathway.milestone: self-healing elastomers and printed soft machines with embedded electronics
pathway.unlocks: long-lived soft devices and cheaper mass production.
